datasets.name: HAPwave_bids
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 8 patients undergoing single pulse electrical stimulation while resting in a hospital bed. The dataset supports investigation of stimulation-driven network interactions in the human limbic system. Data are organized in BIDS with metadata for event timing.
datasets.authors: Ojeda Valencia, G., Gregg, N., Huang, H., Lundstrom, B., Brinkmann, B., Pal Attia1, T.,  Van Gompel, J., Bernstein,M., In, M., Huston, J., Worrell1, G., Miller, K., Hermes, D.

datasets.name: TNO
datasets.description: The TNO dataset is an EEG dataset in BIDS format with HED annotations, authored by Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, and Kevin King. It is a re-deposit of the OpenNeuro dataset ds004660 and is released under a CC0 license.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: Driving with Autonomous Aids
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a semi-automated driving task designed to study human trust in automation (TiA). Participants performed lane maintenance, following-distance control, and pedestrian collision avoidance, with an optional automated assistant of varying quality that they could engage or disengage. Physiological (EEG, EOG, ECG, EDA, gaze) and behavioral measures were recorded to develop metrics that index and predict trust-based decisions.
datasets.authors: Jason Metcalfe, Amar Marathe, Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: Intraoperative recordings of medianus stimulation with low and high impedance ECoG
datasets.description: Intraoperative electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings of median nerve somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) from 10 patients undergoing brain tumor resection in the perirolandic region. Two 4-contact ECoG strips, one low impedance (LoZ) and one high impedance (HiZ), were recorded simultaneously to compare fast ripple and high frequency oscillation detection. The data comprise continuous raw ECoG in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Vasileios Dimakopoulos, Marian Neidert, Johannes Sarnthein

datasets.name: Gaffrey Lab Infant Microstates Reliability
datasets.description: High-density EEG recordings from 48 infants aged 5-10 months who watched relaxing videos while seated on a caregiver's lap. The dataset supports microstate analysis of continuous infant EEG and evaluation of the reliability of microstate measures, and accompanies a tutorial on the analysis pipeline.
datasets.authors: Armen Bagdasarov, Michael S. Gaffrey

datasets.name: Can we dissociate hypervigilance to social threats from altered perceptual decision-making processes in lonely individuals? An exploration with Drift Diffusion Modelling and event-related potentials.
datasets.description: EEG dataset examining whether hypervigilance to social threats in lonely individuals can be dissociated from altered perceptual decision-making. Behavioral data were analysed with Drift Diffusion Modelling and neural responses with event-related potentials. The dataset accompanies a Psychophysiology article on loneliness and social threat processing.
datasets.authors: Szymon Mąka, Marta Chrustowicz, Łukasz Okruszek

datasets.name: Mind in Motion Young Adults Walking Over Uneven Terrain
datasets.description: A multimodal mobile brain/body imaging dataset from 32 young adults walking over uneven terrain at different speeds. It includes high-density dual-layer EEG, neck EMG, IMU acceleration, ground reaction forces, and head models built from T1-weighted MR images. Each participant also completed a seated rest trial, and digitized electrode locations are provided for every subject.
datasets.authors: Chang Liu, Ryan J. Downey, Jacob S. Salminen, Sofia Arvelo Rojas, Erika M. Pliner, Natalie Richer, Jungyun Hwang, Yenisel Cruz-Almeida, Todd M. Manini, Chris J. Hass, Rachael D. Seidler, David J. Clark, Daniel P. Ferris

datasets.name: Intracranial recordings using BCI2000 and the CorTec BrainInterchange
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial recordings acquired in humans using the CorTec BrainInterchange implantable device together with BCI2000 software. It supports the development of an ecosystem of technology and protocols for adaptive neuromodulation research. The data are shared in BIDS format with iEEG recordings.
datasets.authors: F. Mivalt, F. Lampert, M.A. van den Boom, P. Brunner, J. Kim, Andrea Duque-lopez, M. Krakorova, V. Kremen, D. Hermes, G.A. Worrell, K. J. Miller
datasets.bids_version: Brain Imaging Data Structure Specification v1.8.0

datasets.name: The Nencki-Symfonia EEG/ERP dataset
datasets.description: The Nencki-Symfonia EEG/ERP dataset contains high-density EEG recordings from healthy adults performing multiple cognitive tasks and a resting-state protocol. Tasks include an extended multi-source interference task (MSIT+), a three-stimulus oddball task, and a simple reaction task used as a control. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and supports studies of cognitive control, attention, and event-related potentials.
datasets.authors: Dzianok Patrycja, Antonova Ingrida, Wojciechowski Jakub, Dreszer Joanna, Kublik Ewa

datasets.name: Visual Attribute-Specific Contextual Trajectory Paradigm
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 37 healthy adult participants (under 35 years, normal or corrected-to-normal vision) performing a visual contextual trajectory paradigm. In this paradigm, the onset of a bound stimulus violated an established trajectory in brightness, size, or orientation, while control trials contained no violation. The dataset supports investigation of attribute-specific prediction error and expectation signals in visual processing.
datasets.authors: Benjamin Lowe (ben.lowe@mq.edu.au), Jonathan Robinson (jonathan.robinson@monash.edu), Naohide Yamamoto (naohide.yamamoto@qut.edu.au), Hinze Hogendoorn (hinze.hogendoorn@qut.edu.au), Patrick Johnston (dr.pat.johnston@icloud.com)

datasets.name: Registered Replication Report of ERN/Pe Psychometrics
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a registered replication study examining the psychometric properties of the error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe) across multiple response-monitoring tasks. Raw EGI recordings were imported into EEGLAB, recoded into response-locked and stimulus-locked ERN/Pe event labels, and organized in BIDS format. The data support work on the reliability and construct validity of performance-monitoring event-related potentials.
datasets.authors: Peter E. Clayson, Michael J. Larson

datasets.name: LFP during linear track in 6-month old TgF344-AD rats
datasets.description: Local field potential (LFP) recordings collected from TgF344-AD rats, a transgenic model of Alzheimer's disease, at 6 months of age while the animals traversed a linear track. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and supports investigation of hippocampal network activity in early-stage Alzheimer's disease pathology.
datasets.authors: Moradi Faraz, van den Berg Monica, Mirjebreili Morteza, Kosten Lauren, Verhoye Marleen, Amiri Mahmood, Keliris A. Georgios

datasets.name: EEG: RL Task (3-Armed Bandit) with alcohol cues in hazardous drinkers and ctls
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 53 community participants, including hazardous drinkers and controls, performing a reinforcement learning task (3-armed bandit) with alcohol-related versus beverage cue images. The dataset supports investigation of electrophysiological markers of cue-specific exploration in hazardous drinking. Data were collected between 2019 and 2021 at the CRCL at the University of New Mexico.
datasets.authors: Ethan Campbell, James F Cavanagh

datasets.name: IllusionGameEEG_data
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG, physiological (ECG, PPG, respiration) and behavioural recordings from 103 healthy adults aged 21-45, collected in 2022-2023 as part of a larger study. Participants completed an 8-minute eyes-closed resting state, followed by the Illusion Game. In this task they made perceptual judgements about the Ebbinghaus, Müller-Lyer and Vertical-Horizontal illusions, with task difficulty and illusion strength varied. The data are intended for investigating individual sensitivity to visual illusions as a general factor.
datasets.authors: Makowski, Dominique, Te, An-Shu, Jiayi, Zhang, Kirk, Stephanie, Ngoi, Zi Liang

datasets.name: Rest eyes open
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG dataset from 149 participants, including 100 individuals with Parkinson's disease and 49 controls. Recordings were acquired with a 64-channel BrainVision system during two minutes of eyes-open rest. The data support investigation of neural correlates of cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson's disease.
datasets.authors: Arun Singh arun.singh@usd.edu, Rachel Cole rachel-cole@uiowa.edu, Arturo Espinoza arturo-espinoza@uiowa.edu, Jim Cavanagh jcavanagh@unm.edu, Nandakumar Narayanan nandakumar-narayanan@uiowa.edu

datasets.name: Simon-conflict Task.
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 146 participants (98 individuals with Parkinson's disease and 48 controls) performing a Simon conflict task. Stimuli appeared on the left or right side of the screen, and participants responded with a left or right key according to stimulus color. Trials were spatially congruent or incongruent with the response hand. Data were collected alongside other cognitive tasks to study conflict processing and midfrontal activity in Parkinson's disease.
datasets.authors: Arun Singh arun.singh@usd.edu, Rachel Cole rachel-cole@uiowa.edu, Arturo Espinoza arturo-espinoza@uiowa.edu, Jan R Wessel jan-wessel@uiowa.edu, Jim Cavanagh jcavanagh@unm.edu, Nandakumar Narayanan nandakumar-narayanan@uiowa.edu

datasets.name: Interval Timing Task
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 139 participants, 94 with Parkinson's disease and 45 controls, performing an interval timing task. Participants judged short (3 s) and long (7 s) intervals and pressed a spacebar when they thought the target interval had elapsed, while a distractor vowel appeared at random times. The dataset supports research on midfrontal activity and cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson's disease.
datasets.authors: Arun Singh arun.singh@usd.edu, Rachel Cole rachel-cole@uiowa.edu, Arturo Espinoza arturo-espinoza@uiowa.edu, Jan R Wessel jan-wessel@uiowa.edu, Jim Cavanagh jcavanagh@unm.edu, Nandakumar Narayanan nandakumar-narayanan@uiowa.edu

datasets.name: Dataset containing resting EEG for a sample of 103 normal infants in the first year of life
datasets.description: This dataset contains resting-state EEG recordings from 103 normal infants (41 female, 62 male) during the first year of life. A total of 130 recordings were collected, with some infants recorded up to four times, organized into four sessions. It supports the study of normative quantitative EEG, sleep EEG, and functional connectivity during early brain development.
datasets.authors: Thalía Harmony (Neurodevelopment Research Unit; Instituto de Neurobiología; Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México), Gloria Otero-Ojeda (Facultad de Medicina; Universidad Autónoma del Estado de México), Eduardo Aubert (Centro de Neurociencias de Cuba), Thalía Fernández (Neurodevelopment Research Unit; Instituto de Neurobiología; Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México), Lourdes Cubero-Rego (Neurodevelopment Research Unit; Instituto de Neurobiología; Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México)

datasets.name: Cross-modal Oddball Task.
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 146 participants (98 with Parkinson's disease and 48 controls) performing a cross-modal oddball task collected between 2017 and 2021. Each trial presented simultaneous visual and auditory pre-cues, either standard or oddball, followed by a directional arrow GO cue requiring a response. The dataset supports investigation of midfrontal neural activity and cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson's disease.
datasets.authors: Arun Singh arun.singh@usd.edu, Rachel Cole rachel-cole@uiowa.edu, Arturo Espinoza arturo-espinoza@uiowa.edu, Jan R Wessel jan-wessel@uiowa.edu, Jim Cavanagh jcavanagh@unm.edu, Nandakumar Narayanan nandakumar-narayanan@uiowa.edu

datasets.name: The effects of sham hypnosis techniques
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 52 participants (39 female) who took part in a 2x2 balanced placebo study of hypnosis. Each participant received conventional and unconventional (placebo) hypnotic inductions, each framed either as hypnosis or as a control relaxation technique. Data were recorded with a 64-channel EasyCap system and include pre- and post-hypnosis closed-eyes resting baselines. The dataset supports investigation of how framing affects hypnotic depth and its electrophysiological correlates.
datasets.authors: Zoltan Kekecs, Kyra Girán, Vanda Vizkievicz, Anna Lutoskin, Yeganeh Farahzadi

datasets.name: Vicarious touch: overlapping neural patterns between seeing and feeling touch
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings from people with and without vicarious touch experiences. Participants either felt touch to their fingers or watched matched videos of touch to another person's fingers. It was collected to test, using time-resolved multivariate pattern analysis, whether seen touch evokes neural representations that overlap with first-hand touch. Raw and processed data, code and stimuli are included.
datasets.authors: Sophie Smit, Denise Moerel, Regine Zopf, Anina N Rich

datasets.name: Illusion of Agency over Electrically-Actuated Movements
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating the sense of agency over movements produced by electrical muscle stimulation (electrically-actuated movements). It examines the illusion of agency when involuntary, externally actuated movements are experienced, and provides raw EEG recordings organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: John Veillette, Pedro Lopes, Howard Nusbaum

datasets.name: Forced Picture Naming Task
datasets.description: EEG dataset recorded during a forced picture naming task in sixteen native French-speaking men aged 18 to 70. Participants named black-and-white line drawings from the Snodgrass & Vanderwart corpus, with each trial comprising a pre-stimulus baseline, a post-stimulus phase, and a naming phase. The preprocessed data were used to characterize spatiotemporal EEG dynamics with optical flow patterns.
datasets.authors: V. Volpert, B. Xu, A. Tchechmedjiev, S. Harispe, A. Aksenov, Q. Mesnildrey and A. Beuter

datasets.name: iEEG on children during slow wave sleep
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 114 children obtained during slow wave sleep. It was curated to accompany a manuscript by Sakakura et al. (in preparation), and electrode coordinates are provided in MNI305 space. Analysis code in Matlab is available from the authors' GitHub repository.
datasets.authors: Kazuki Sakakura, Naoto Kuroda, Masaki Sonoda, Takumi Mitsuhashi, Ethan Firestone, Aimee F. Luat, Neena I. Marupudi, Sandeep Sood, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: Multimodal EEG-fNIRS data from patients undergoing general anesthesia
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous multimodal EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings from patients undergoing general anesthesia. It is organized in BIDS format and supports research on brain activity and hemodynamics during anesthetic administration and changes in consciousness.
datasets.authors: Catalina Saini Ferrón, Gabriela Vargas González, Carlos Valle Araya

datasets.name: EEG: Probabilistic Selection Task (PST) + PST with Cabergoline Challenge
datasets.description: EEG recordings from a Probabilistic Selection Task (PST) collected in two studies: 80 healthy participants plus 5 pilot placebo sessions, and a double-blind cabergoline (1.25 mg) challenge study with 27 completers. Data were collected circa 2012-2013 at Brown University and share a sample with a previously published study on conflict as an implicit cost in reinforcement learning. The dataset supports research on reinforcement learning, dopamine, and feedback processing.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Michael J Frank

datasets.name: Changes in behavioral priority influence the accessibility of working memory content - Experiment 1
datasets.description: Preprocessed EEG data from Experiment 1 of a study examining how changes in behavioral priority affect the accessibility of working memory content. The dataset is provided in BIDS format as EEGLAB .set files. Analysis scripts for the project are hosted on OSF.
datasets.authors: Edward Ester, Paige Pytel

datasets.name: Changes in behavioral priority influence the accessibility of working memory content - Experiment 2
datasets.description: Preprocessed EEG data from Experiment 2 of a study on how changes in behavioral priority influence the accessibility of working memory content. The dataset is provided in BIDS format as EEGLAB .set files. Analysis scripts for the project are hosted on OSF.
datasets.authors: Edward Ester, Paige Pytel

datasets.name: Internal selective attention is delayed by competition between endogenous and exogenous factors
datasets.description: This dataset contains preprocessed EEG data from a study of internal selective attention, examining how competition between endogenous and exogenous factors delays the deployment of attention to internal (working memory) representations. Data are provided in BIDS format as .set files with accompanying behavioral summary files for alignment with the EEG.
datasets.authors: Edward Ester, Asal Nouri

datasets.name: EEG recordings for semantic decoding of imagined animals and tools during auditory imagery task
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 7 participants performing an auditory imagery task, in which they imagined the sounds made by objects from the semantic categories of animals and tools for 5 seconds. It supports research on semantic decoding and brain-computer interfacing. Recordings were made with a 64-channel BioSemi system, with additional EOG, physiological, and respiration channels.
datasets.authors: Milan Rybář, Riccardo Poli, Ian Daly

datasets.name: EEG: Alcohol imagery reinforcement learning task with light and heavy drinker participants
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 54 community participants classified as light or heavy drinkers performing an affective-state reinforcement learning task involving alcohol imagery. The dataset supports investigation of reward-related neural responses, such as the reward positivity, in relation to drinking behavior. Data were collected between 2019 and 2021.
datasets.authors: Garima Singh, James F Cavanagh

datasets.name: Simultaneous EEG and fNIRS recordings for semantic decoding of imagined animals and tools
datasets.description: This dataset provides simultaneous EEG and fNIRS recordings from 12 participants performing a silent naming task and three sensory-based imagery tasks (visual, auditory, tactile) on objects from the semantic categories of animals and tools. It supports research on semantic decoding and brain-computer interfacing. Stimulus images and example Python scripts for loading the data with MNE and MNE-BIDS are included.
datasets.authors: Milan Rybář, Riccardo Poli, Ian Daly

datasets.name: Deception_data
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG, physiological, and behavioural recordings collected in 2020 from 44 healthy adults aged 21-40. It includes eyes-closed resting-state recordings and two tasks: a spontaneous deception task (a gambling game with self-reported dice-roll predictions) and a cognitive control task battery. The battery covers processing speed, response selection, response inhibition, and conflict resolution.
datasets.authors: Makowski, Dominique, Pham, Tam, Lau, Zen Juen

datasets.name: Real World Table Tennis
datasets.description: A multimodal dataset of high-density, dual-layer EEG, neck EMG, inertial measurement unit acceleration, T1 structural MRI, and video recorded from 25 participants playing real-world table tennis. Each participant played 60 minutes of table tennis against a ball machine and a human player, plus a 10-minute standing baseline. Processed data include ICA decompositions and dipole models, with raw data in the sourcedata folder.
datasets.authors: Amanda Studnicki, Daniel P. Ferris

datasets.name: Anticipatory differences between Attention and Expectation
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating anticipatory neural differences between attention and expectation. The recordings were collected by a research group led by Maria Ruz and are organized in BIDS format. The dataset is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds004502).
datasets.authors: Jose M. G. Penalver, David Lopez-Garcia, Blanca Aguado-Lopez, Carlos Gonzalez-Garcia, Maria Ruz

datasets.name: ABSeqMEG
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from participants listening to 16-item binary sound sequences of varying complexity, used to test a language-of-thought account of compression in human working memory. Sequences were defined by minimal description length (transition probabilities, chunking, or nested structures), and occasional deviant sounds probed participants' knowledge of each sequence. The data accompany a study reporting that MEG and fMRI responses scale with sequence complexity.
datasets.authors: Samuel Planton*, Fosca Al Roumi*, Liping Wang, Stanislas Dehaene

datasets.name: PES - Pandemic Emergency Scenario
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a complex, strategic decision-making pandemic emergency scenario in which nine participants, paired with an artificial agent, allocated limited resources (medicines, personnel) to cities shown on a map. Participants reported their confidence in each decision across 64 sequences. Recordings combine 64-channel EEG with ECG and EOG channels and behavioural responses, supporting research on decision making, confidence and human-machine teaming.
datasets.authors: Tasos Papastylianou, Rodrigo Ramele, Luca Citi, Caterina Cinel, Riccardo Poli

datasets.name: sEEG Forced Two-Choice Task
datasets.description: This dataset contains stereoelectroencephalography (sEEG) recordings from patients performing a forced two-choice response task in the epilepsy monitoring unit at Oregon Health & Science University. The data were analyzed in collaboration with the University of Oregon and were used to characterize movement-related oscillations in intracranial recordings. It is organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Alexander P. Rockhill, Alessandra Mantovani, Brittany Stedelin, Admed M. Raslan, Nicole C. Swann

datasets.name: EEG and motion capture data set for a full-body/joystick rotation task
datasets.description: A mobile brain/body imaging (MoBI) dataset combining 157-channel EEG and full-body motion capture from 20 healthy adults performing a spatial heading-change task. Participants followed a moving sphere and returned to their initial heading either by physically rotating on the spot or by using a joystick with a 2D desktop display. The dataset supports investigation of human cortical dynamics during full-body rotation and is formatted according to BIDS.
datasets.authors: Gramann, K., Hohlefeld, F.U., Gehrke, L., Klug, M

datasets.name: Electrical stimulation of temporal and limbic circuitry produces distinct responses in human ventral temporal cortex
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG recordings from five patients undergoing clinical monitoring at the Mayo Clinic, collected during single pulse electrical stimulation. The dataset supports identification of distinct basis profile curves in human ventral temporal cortex evoked by stimulation of temporal and limbic circuitry. Analysis code is available in an accompanying GitHub repository.
datasets.authors: Harvey Huang, Nicholas M Gregg, Gabriela Ojeda Valencia, Benjamin H Brinkmann, Brian N Lundstrom, Gregory A Worrell, Kai J Miller, Dora Hermes

datasets.name: The BMI-HDEEG dataset 4
datasets.description: A high-density scalp EEG dataset recorded during sensorimotor rhythm-based brain-computer interface (BCI) operation. The dataset is intended to support research on BCI performance, sensorimotor rhythm modulation, and EEG signal analysis. It is part of the BMI-HDEEG series and is accompanied by a data descriptor article and sample analysis code.
datasets.authors: Seitaro Iwama, Masumi Morishige, Yoshikazu Takahashi, Ryotaro Hirose, Midori Kodama, Junichi Ushiba

datasets.name: The BMI-HDEEG dataset 3
datasets.description: A high-density scalp EEG dataset recorded while participants performed sensorimotor rhythm-based brain-computer interface (BCI) tasks. The recordings support investigation of sensorimotor rhythm modulation and BCI control, as well as development of decoding and analysis methods. It is the third dataset in the BMI-HDEEG series.
datasets.authors: Seitaro Iwama, Masumi Morishige, Yoshikazu Takahashi, Ryotaro Hirose, Midori Kodama, Junichi Ushiba

datasets.name: The BMI-HDEEG dataset 2
datasets.description: A high-density scalp EEG dataset recorded while participants performed sensorimotor rhythm-based brain-computer interface (BCI) tasks. The recordings support research on motor imagery decoding, variability in BCI performance, and neural correlates of sensorimotor rhythm modulation. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and accompanied by sample analysis code.
datasets.authors: Seitaro Iwama, Masumi Morishige, Yoshikazu Takahashi, Ryotaro Hirose, Midori Kodama, Junichi Ushiba

datasets.name: The BMI-HDEEG dataset 1
datasets.description: A high-density scalp EEG dataset recorded while participants performed sensorimotor rhythm-based brain-computer interface (BCI) tasks. The recordings support investigation of sensorimotor rhythm modulation and BCI control, as well as development of decoding and analysis methods. Sample analysis code is provided in an accompanying repository.
datasets.authors: Seitaro Iwama, Masumi Morishige, Yoshikazu Takahashi, Ryotaro Hirose, Midori Kodama, Junichi Ushiba

datasets.name: EEG responses to continuous naturalistic speech
datasets.description: This dataset contains 128-channel EEG recordings from healthy, neurotypical adults listening to naturalistic continuous speech, specifically segments of an audiobook version of "The Old Man and the Sea". It combines data from two earlier studies on cortical entrainment to speech and on semantic processing. It includes the audio stimuli and forced-aligned word and phoneme timing files, supporting research on speech and language processing.
datasets.authors: Giovanni M Di Liberto, Michael P Broderick, Ole Bialas, Edmund C Lalor

datasets.name: Somatosensory evoked potentials in the human spinal cord to mixed and sensory nerve stimulation
datasets.description: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), electrospinography (ESG), electroneurography (ENG) and electromyography (EMG) recordings from 26 participants, together with electrocardiographic and respiratory signals. Somatosensory evoked potentials were elicited by mixed nerve stimulation (median and tibial nerves) and sensory nerve stimulation of fingers and toes, alongside a resting-state condition with eyes open. ESG electrode positions are provided for each participant. The study was pre-registered on OSF.
datasets.authors: Birgit Nierula, Tilman Stephani, Merve Kaptan, André Moruaux, Burkhard Maess, Gabriel Curio, Vadim V. Nikulin, Falk Eippert
datasets.eeg_reference: EEG: RM (right mastoid); ESG: TH6 (over 6th thoracic vertebra); ECG: ECGN (below right clavicle), ENG: (1) left Erb's Point: EPN (ref placed over right Erb's point), (2) Biceps: BicepsN (approx. 3 cm proximal to active electrode), (3) Knee: kneeMN (located approx. 3cm proximal to kneeM, all knee channels had the same reference);

datasets.name: Somatosensory evoked potentials in the human spinal cord to mixed nerve stimulation
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), electrospinography (ESG), electroneurography (ENG), and electromyography (EMG) recordings from 40 participants, together with electrocardiographic and respiratory signals. Four conditions were recorded: resting state with eyes open, mixed median nerve stimulation, mixed tibial nerve stimulation, and alternating median/tibial stimulation. ESG electrode positions are provided for each participant. The study was pre-registered on OSF.
datasets.authors: Birgit Nierula, Tilman Stephani, Merve Kaptan, André Moruaux, Burkhard Maess, Gabriel Curio, Vadim V. Nikulin, Falk Eippert
datasets.eeg_reference: EEG: RM (right mastoid); ESG: TH6 (over 6th thoracic vertebra); ECG: ECGN (below right clavicle), ENG: (1) left Erb's Point: EPN (ref placed over right Erb's point), (2) Biceps: BicepsN (approx. 3 cm proximal to active electrode), (3) Knee: kneeMN (located approx. 3cm proximal to kneeM, all knee channels had the same reference);

datasets.name: Intraoperative EEG dataset during medianus-tibialis stimulation with 8 different rates
datasets.description: Intraoperative EEG recordings of somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) elicited by median and tibial nerve stimulation at eight different stimulus repetition rates. The dataset includes 14 adult and 4 pediatric subjects, with continuous EEG split into sessions by nerve and side and into runs by stimulation rate. Processed derivatives are also provided. The data were used to assess how stimulation rate affects the signal-to-noise ratio of short-duration SEP recordings.
datasets.authors: Giorgio Selmin, Vasileios Dimakopoulos, Niklaus Krayenbühl, Luca Regli, Johannes Sarnthein

datasets.name: PRIOS
datasets.description: The PRIOS dataset contains electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from 6 patients aged 13-53 years. Cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) were elicited by single pulse electrical stimulation (SPES), both in the awake patient during clinical routine and under general propofol anesthesia in the operating room. The data support investigation of how propofol affects local effective brain networks.
datasets.authors: van Blooijs D, Blok S, Huiskamp GJM, Leijten FSS
datasets.bids_version: Brain Imaging Data Structure Specification v1.6.0

datasets.name: Blink-Pause-Relation (Competing Speaker Paradigm)
datasets.description: This dataset pools EOG recordings from two earlier studies (20 participants from Jaeger et al., 2020 and 21 from Holtze et al., 2021) that used a competing-speaker paradigm. Participants attended to either the left or the right of two simultaneously presented audio books. The dataset supports analysis of the relation between eye blinks and speech pauses.
datasets.authors: Bjoern Holtze, Marc Rosenkranz, Martin Bleichner, Stefan Debener

datasets.name: Features-EEG
datasets.description: Electroencephalography recordings from 16 participants viewing rapid serial visual presentation streams of Gabor-like stimuli. The dataset was collected to study the temporal dynamics of visual feature coding and integration in perception. Stimuli were presented at 6.67 Hz and 20 Hz while participants performed an orthogonal fixation colour change detection task.
datasets.authors: Grootswagers, Tijl, Robinson, Amanda, Shatek, Sofia, Carlson, Thomas

datasets.name: Subcortical responses to music and speech are alike while cortical responses diverge
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 22 analyzed normal-hearing adults (24 enrolled) listening to clicks, music, and speech, collected to derive auditory brainstem responses (ABR) from continuous natural stimuli by deconvolution. The dataset compares subcortical and cortical responses to six music genres and six speech types. Raw BrainVision EEG files, event annotations, and the audio stimuli are included.
datasets.authors: Tong Shan, Madeline S. Cappelloni, Ross K. Maddox

datasets.name: Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2017 (EESM17)
datasets.description: The Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2017 (EESM17) dataset contains overnight recordings from 9 healthy participants, made at the participants' homes. Recordings combine partial polysomnography (scalp EEG, EOG, chin EMG) with 14 ear-EEG electrodes. A pre-sleep wake recording and a night-time sleep recording are provided for each subject, with sleep scoring beginning at lights out.
datasets.authors: Kaare B. Mikkelsen, David B. Villadsen, Laura Birch, Marit Otto, Preben Kidmose

datasets.name: Symmetry perception and affective responses: a combined EEG/EMG study
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous EEG and facial EMG recordings examining symmetry perception and associated affective responses. Participants viewed visual patterns and, after stimulus offset, reported whether each pattern was regular (symmetric) or random. It supports investigation of neural and psychophysiological correlates of the processing of visual symmetry.
datasets.authors: Makin, A. D. J, Wilton, M. M, Pecchinenda, A., Bertamini, M.

datasets.name: FLUX: A pipeline for MEG analysis
datasets.description: This dataset contains MEG recordings accompanying the FLUX pipeline, a workflow for analysing magnetoencephalography data. It provides example data organised in the BIDS format so that users can follow and reproduce the pipeline's processing and analysis steps.
datasets.authors: Oscar Ferrante, Ling Liu, Tamas Minarik, Urszula Gorska, Tara Ghafari, Huan Luo, Ole Jensen

datasets.name: ToonFaces
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating whether images of stylized (cartoon-like) faces with exaggerated visual features improve event-related potential (ERP) correlates of emotion relative to ordinary human faces. The stylized faces elicit an enhanced N170 component associated with facial recognition encoding. The findings suggest that consistent stimulus transformations could improve affect detection from EEG in affective brain-computer interface design.
datasets.authors: Luis Alberto Barradas Chacón, Selina C. Wriessnegger

datasets.name: Mood Manipulation and PST, Experiment 2
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a reinforcement learning study of 50 healthy controls, 25 tested after a sad mood manipulation and 25 after a happy mood manipulation. Participants completed a probabilistic selection task with training and testing phases. The task was adapted from a Parkinsonism reinforcement learning paradigm, and the mood manipulation was delivered before each training block.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Trevor C J Jackson

datasets.name: Mood Manipulation and PST, Experiment 1
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a reinforcement learning task (probabilistic selection task, PST) performed by 50 healthy controls after either a sad or neutral mood manipulation (25 per group). The task has a training phase and a testing phase, and the mood induction took place separately beforehand. Data were collected between 2019 and 2021 at the Cognitive Rhythms and Computation Lab, University of New Mexico.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Trevor C J Jackson

datasets.name: EEG Semantic Imagination and Perception Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains 124-channel EEG recordings from 13 participants who imagined and perceived stimuli from three modalities: visual pictorial, visual orthographic, and auditory. Stimuli came from three semantically dissimilar categories (guitar, flower, penguin). Raw, pre-processed, and epoched versions of the data are provided to support research on semantic decoding from EEG.
datasets.authors: Holly Wilson, Mohammad Golbabaee, Michael Proulx, Eamonn O'Neill

datasets.name: Reward gain and punishment avoidance reversal learning
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants performing two reversal learning tasks that differ in reinforcer type: monetary reward versus avoidance of an aversive loud white noise burst. In the reward task, positive feedback meant a gain of 10 cents and negative feedback meant no gain. In the punishment task, positive feedback meant the noise burst was successfully avoided and negative feedback meant the noise was delivered. Noise intensity was titrated per participant to match the motivational value of the 10 cent reward.
datasets.authors: Christopher Stolz, Alan Pickering, Erik M. Mueller

datasets.name: Large Spanish EEG
datasets.description: A large EEG dataset of 60 sessions from 56 healthy Spanish-speaking participants, recorded with 64 channels during perception and silent production of 30 everyday Spanish sentences. It was collected to support subject-independent decoding of perceived sentences with deep neural networks, with the aim of enabling speech neuroprostheses that need no patient-specific training data.
datasets.authors: Carlos Valle Araya, Carolina Mendez-Orellana, Maria Rodriguez-Fernandez

datasets.name: Sustained Neural Representations of Personally Familiar People and Places During Cued Recall
datasets.description: This dataset contains magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from participants performing a cued recall task involving personally familiar people and places. It was collected to examine sustained neural representations of familiar people and places during recall. The data are organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Alexis Kidder(*), Anna Corriveau(*), Lina Teichmann, Susan Wardle, Chris Baker, [(*) = equal contribution]

datasets.name: Auditory single word recognition in MEG
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from participants performing auditory single word recognition. The dataset accompanies a study of auditory word comprehension in isolated words and is organized in BIDS format. Stimuli and TextGrids come from the Massive Auditory Lexical Decision database.
datasets.authors: Phoebe Gaston, Christian Brodbeck, Colin Phillips, Ellen Lau

datasets.name: Steer the Ship
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 21 participants performing a continuous control task in which they steered a ship, shown as a rotating arrow, toward a target using left and right key presses. The underlying dynamics were unstable, based on the pole-and-cart problem. Participants were cued before each round about the level of controller noise and environmental noise (wind), giving four noise conditions. Event triggers mark cues, round start, button presses, crashes, successes, and points display.
datasets.authors: Cameron D. Hassall, Yan Yan, Laurence T. Hunt

datasets.name: Continuous Feedback Processing
datasets.description: EEG dataset from twenty-one participants performing a continuous feedback learning task in which they predicted the final level of an animated rising bar. Cues (gnomes) differed in how predictable the outcome was (highly predictable, somewhat predictable, unpredictable), enabling study of feedback processing under varying outcome uncertainty. Points were awarded according to the accuracy of each guess.
datasets.authors: Cameron D. Hassall, Yan Yan, Laurence T. Hunt

datasets.name: Encoding of Sound Source Elevation in Human Cortex
datasets.description: This EEG dataset contains recordings from two experiments in which participants listened to noise bursts presented from loudspeakers at different elevations in a hemi-anechoic chamber. Experiment 1 was a deviant detection task with adapter and probe sounds, and Experiment 2 was a one-back localization task. Participants first completed a behavioral test of their ability to localize elevated sound sources. The dataset supports research on how sound source elevation is encoded in human auditory cortex.
datasets.authors: Ole Bialas, Marc Schoenwiesner, Burkhard Maess

datasets.name: Rotation-tolerant representations elucidate the time course of high-level object processing
datasets.description: This dataset contains electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 16 participants viewing object images presented in eight different 2-D rotations. Images were shown in rapid serial visual streams at two presentation rates (5 Hz and 20 Hz). The data support investigation of the time course of rotation-tolerant, high-level object representations in the human brain.
datasets.authors: Denise Moerel, Tijl Grootswagers, Amanda K. Robinson, Patrick Engeler, Alex O. Holcombe, Thomas A. Carlson

datasets.name: amnoise
datasets.description: MEG recordings from a single infant subject in the ILABS amnoise dataset, collected in the context of research on infants at risk for dyslexia. The recordings relate to auditory processing during the linguistic sensitive period for native phoneme learning. The data are organized in BIDS format and were converted using MNE-BIDS.
datasets.authors: Maria Mittag, Eric Larson, Maggie Clarke, Samu Taulu, Patricia K. Kuhl

datasets.name: CCEP ECoG dataset across age 4-51
datasets.description: This dataset contains cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) recorded with electrocorticography (ECoG) during single pulse electrical stimulation in 74 patients aged 4-51 years. It was collected at the University Medical Center Utrecht as part of the RESPect epilepsy surgery registry and supports investigation of how signal transmission speed in the human brain develops with age. Data are organized in BIDS with electrode positions labeled by Destrieux atlas and transformed to MNI152 space.
datasets.authors: D. van Blooijs, M.A. van den Boom, J.F. van der Aar, G.J.M. Huiskamp, G. Castegnaro, M. Demuru, W.J.E.M. Zweiphenning, P. van Eijsden, K. J. Miller, F.S.S. Leijten, D. Hermes
datasets.bids_version: Brain Imaging Data Structure Specification v1.6.0

datasets.name: Temporal Scaling
datasets.description: EEG recordings from twenty participants who learned three temporal intervals (short, medium, long). Two randomly interleaved subtasks were used: a Production task, in which participants produced a target interval, and a Perception task, in which they judged whether a computer-generated interval was correct. Visual feedback (checkmark or x) followed both tasks. The dataset supports investigation of temporal scaling of human scalp-recorded potentials.
datasets.authors: Cameron D. Hassall, Jack Harley, Nils Kolling, Laurence T. Hunt

datasets.name: Bimodal dataset on Inner speech
datasets.description: A bimodal dataset of EEG and fMRI recordings acquired nonsimultaneously during inner-speech production in four healthy, right-handed participants. Participants performed an inner-speech task with eight words from two categories, social and numeric, with 40 trials per word, giving 320 trials per modality per participant. The dataset is intended to support inner speech recognition and brain-computer interfaces for speech prostheses.
datasets.authors: Foteini Liwicki, Vibha Gupta, Rajkumar Saini, Kanjar De, Nosheen Abid, Sumit Rakesh, Scott Wellington, Holly Wilson, Marcus Liwicki, Johan Eriksson

datasets.name: Visual ECoG dataset
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (ECoG) recordings from 14 epilepsy patients implanted with clinical surface and depth electrodes, with two patients also carrying high-density research grids. Participants viewed grayscale pattern stimuli and color images of several categories. Stimuli varied in spatial and temporal properties, including pRF mapping bars, spatial and temporal patterns, and six-category localizers. Pre-implantation T1 MRI, FreeSurfer surface reconstructions and derivative broadband and preprocessed data are included.
datasets.authors: Iris Groen, Kenichi Yuasa, Amber Brands, Giovanni Piantoni, Stephanie Montenegro, Adeen Flinker, Sasha Devore, Orrin Devinsky, Werner Doyle, Patricia Dugan, Daniel Friedman, Nick Ramsey, Natalia Petridou, Jonathan Winawer

datasets.name: Effects of Forward and Backward Span Trainings on Working Memory: Evidence from a Randomized, Controlled Trial
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG/ERP recordings from a randomized controlled trial comparing forward span training, backward span training, and no-intervention control groups on working memory. Recordings were collected at pre-, mid-, and post-test while participants performed a distractor version of the change detection task, and behavioral data were collected from additional change detection and suppress tasks. The data support analyses of working memory maintenance and interference control, indexed by Kmax and contralateral delay activity (CDA).
datasets.authors: Yang Li (data and curation), Wenjin Fu (data), Qiumei Zhang (data), Xiongying Chen (data), Xiaohong Li (data), Boqi Du (data), Xiaoxiang Deng (data), Feng Ji (curation), Qi Dong (curation), Susanne M. Jaeggi (curation), Chuansheng Chen (curation), Jun Li (data and curation)

datasets.name: Drum Trainer
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 21 participants learning to play two drumming patterns at three tempos (fast, medium, slow) by pressing keys on a standard keyboard. Each key press triggered visual feedback indicating whether the response was early, on time, or late, with the timing window adapted trial by trial so that about half of responses were on time. The dataset supports study of feedback-based motor timing and learning.
datasets.authors: Cameron D. Hassall, Yan Yan, Laurence T. Hunt

datasets.name:
Effect of obesity on inhibitory control in preadolescents during stop-signal 
task. An event-related potentials study
datasets.description: This dataset contains 128-channel EEG recordings from fifty-seven obese and non-obese preadolescents performing a stop-signal task. It was collected to examine how obesity affects inhibitory control, as indexed by event-related potentials. Participant data include age, gender, body mass index, and weight status.
datasets.authors: Graciela C. Alatorre-Cruz, Heather Downs, Darcy Hagood, Seth T. Sorensen, D. Keith Williams, Linda Larson-Prior

datasets.name: A test-retest resting and cognitive state EEG dataset
datasets.description: This dataset provides test-retest EEG recordings from 60 participants across three experimental sessions. It includes resting states (eyes closed, eyes open) and cognitive states (subtraction, music, memory). Recordings are accompanied by measures of sleep, emotion, mental health, and mind-wandering.
datasets.authors: Yulin Wang, Wei Duan, Lihong Ding, Debo Dong, Xu Lei

datasets.name: OpenBMI SSVEP EEG dataset (Lee et al. 2019)
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted derivative of the OpenBMI SSVEP EEG dataset (Lee et al. 2019), converted via the MOABB framework for standardized BCI benchmarking. It contains 62-channel EEG recorded at 1000 Hz from 54 participants over two sessions, with a four-class steady-state visually evoked potential paradigm (21,600 trials of 4 s each). The data support analysis of SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces and BCI illiteracy.
datasets.authors: [Unspecified1], [Unspecified2], Min-Ho Lee, O-Yeon Kwon, Yong-Jeong Kim, Hong-Kyung Kim, Young-Eun Lee, John Williamson, Siamac Fazli, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study A — P300 BCI EEG dataset (13 healthy subjects, Mainsah et al. 2025)
datasets.description: A derivative P300 brain-computer interface dataset containing 32-channel EEG recordings from 13 healthy subjects, each with one session, performing a visual speller task with a 6x6 checkerboard stimulus paradigm. Target and non-target events are annotated with HED 8.4.0 and processed with the MOABB framework. It is Study A of the BigP3BCI collection, the largest public P300 BCI dataset.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Visual object ERP EEG dataset (Kaneshiro et al. 2015)
datasets.description: A visual event-related potential dataset of 124-channel EEG recorded from 10 healthy participants viewing photographs from six object categories (human body, human face, animal body, animal face, fruit/vegetable, inanimate object). It contains 5,184 trials, with 72 images per category shown for 500 ms with a 750 ms interstimulus interval. The data support research on neural object representations through single-trial EEG classification and representational similarity analysis, and are distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Blair Kaneshiro, Marcos Perreau Guimaraes, Hyung-Suk Kim, Anthony M. Norcia, Patrick Suppes

datasets.name: P300 BCI EEG dataset (Chailloux Peguero et al. 2020)
datasets.description: A P300 brain-computer interface EEG dataset from 19 healthy participants, each recorded across 3 sessions. The study examines how visual stimulation conditions, standard flash versus cartoon face stimuli, affect single-option P300-BCI performance across grid sizes of 4 to 9 symbols. Recordings use an 8-channel montage sampled at 256 Hz and include target and non-target event labels.
datasets.authors: J. David Chailloux Peguero, Omar Mendoza-Montoya, Javier M. Antelis

datasets.name: Imagined speech EEG dataset — vowels condition (Nguyen et al. 2017)
datasets.description: Preprocessed 64-channel EEG recordings from 8 healthy participants performing imagined speech of three vowel phonemes (a, i, u) in response to auditory and visual cues. The dataset was re-packaged in BIDS format from the MOABB collection and supports decoding of imagined speech with Riemannian manifold features and relevance vector machine classification.
datasets.authors: Chuong H. Nguyen, George K. Karavas, Panagiotis Artemiadis

datasets.name: Imagined Speech EEG database — Spanish vowels and commands (Pressel et al. 2016)
datasets.description: An open-access EEG database of imagined speech recorded from 15 healthy Spanish-speaking adults. Participants imagined 11 classes, comprising 5 Spanish vowels and 6 directional commands, while 6-channel EEG was recorded at 1024 Hz. Trials lasted 4 s with a 3 s imagery window, and the data were bandpass filtered (2-45 Hz). The dataset supports brain-computer interface and imagined speech classification research and is redistributed in BIDS format via the MOABB collection.
datasets.authors: German A. Pressel Coretto, Ivan E. Gareis, Hugo Leonardo Rufiner

datasets.name: Imagined speech EEG dataset — short words condition (Nguyen et al. 2017)
datasets.description: Preprocessed 64-channel EEG recordings from 6 healthy participants performing imagined speech of three short words (out, in, up), cued by auditory and visual stimuli. The dataset contains 1800 trials of a single session, analyzed in the source study with Riemannian manifold covariance features and relevance vector machines for brain-computer interface applications. It is re-hosted in BIDS format from the MOABB benchmark collection.
datasets.authors: Chuong H. Nguyen, George K. Karavas, Panagiotis Artemiadis

datasets.name: Imagined speech EEG dataset — long words condition (Nguyen et al. 2017)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from six healthy participants performing imagined speech of long words, comprising two word classes (cooperate and independent), with 64 channels recorded at 256 Hz. Trials were cued by auditory beeps and visual cues, and the data were analyzed with Riemannian manifold covariance features and relevance vector machines for brain-computer interface classification. The dataset is re-hosted in BIDS format from the MOABB benchmark collection.
datasets.authors: Chuong H. Nguyen, George K. Karavas, Panagiotis Artemiadis

datasets.name: BCI Competition 2020 Track 4 — Upper-limb grasping motor imagery
datasets.description: A preprocessed derivative EEG dataset from BCI Competition 2020 Track 4, containing motor imagery recordings of three right-arm grasping tasks (cylindrical, spherical, lumbrical) from 15 healthy participants across three sessions. It provides 60-channel EEG at 250 Hz with 450 trials per subject and 4 s motor imagery epochs. The dataset is intended for evaluating session-to-session transfer learning in brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Ji-Hoon Jeong, Jeong-Hyun Cho, Young-Eun Lee, Seo-Hyun Lee, Gi-Hwan Shin, Young-Seok Kweon, Jose del R. Millan, Klaus-Robert Muller, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: Imagined speech EEG dataset — short and long words (Nguyen et al. 2017)
datasets.description: Preprocessed 64-channel EEG recordings from six healthy participants performing imagined speech of a short word ('in') versus a long word ('cooperate'). The data were band-pass and notch filtered and cleaned of EOG artifacts. They were used to classify imagined speech with Riemannian manifold covariance features and relevance vector machines for brain-computer interface applications. The dataset is re-hosted in BIDS format through the MOABB benchmark collection.
datasets.authors: Chuong H. Nguyen, George K. Karavas, Panagiotis Artemiadis

datasets.name: BEETL Competition 2021 Motor Imagery Dataset A — transfer learning benchmark
datasets.description: Beetl2021-A is a preprocessed four-class motor imagery EEG dataset (rest, left hand, right hand, feet) from Task 2 of the BEETL Competition at NeurIPS 2021. It contains 63-channel recordings at 500 Hz from healthy participants playing an online BCI racing game (Cybathlon2020IC), with 1490 trials of 4 s each in a single session. It serves as a benchmark for transfer learning and domain adaptation across heterogeneous EEG datasets and subjects, and is re-hosted in BIDS format via the MOABB pipeline.
datasets.authors: [Unspecified1], [Unspecified2]

datasets.name: BCI Competition 2020 Track 5 — ERP during walking (scalp, ear-EEG, and IMU)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 15 healthy participants performing a visual P300 oddball task while walking on a treadmill at 1.6 m/s, released as BCI Competition 2020 Track 5. The dataset combines 46-channel scalp EEG, 14-channel ear-EEG, 4 EOG channels, and 6 inertial measurement unit channels. It is designed to evaluate brain-computer interface performance under ambulatory conditions, with trials divided temporally into training, validation, and test sets.
datasets.authors: Ji-Hoon Jeong, Jeong-Hyun Cho, Young-Eun Lee, Seo-Hyun Lee, Gi-Hwan Shin, Young-Seok Kweon, Jose del R. Millan, Klaus-Robert Muller, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: BNCI 2020-001 Reach-and-Grasp Electrode Comparison EEG dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from healthy participants performing self-initiated palmar and lateral reach-and-grasp actions, acquired simultaneously across three recording systems: gel-based laboratory EEG, water-based mobile EEG, and dry-electrode mobile EEG. The dataset supports investigation of the feasibility of decoding natural reach-and-grasp movement-related cortical potentials across EEG acquisition modalities for brain-computer interface applications. It is distributed in BIDS format as part of the MOABB benchmark collection.
datasets.authors: Andreas Schwarz, Carlos Escolano, Luis Montesano, Gernot R. Müller-Putz

datasets.name: Multi-session longitudinal motor imagery EEG dataset (Kumar et al. 2024)
datasets.description: A longitudinal motor imagery EEG dataset from 18 BCI-naive participants recorded across six sessions (one offline, five online) with 22 EEG channels at 512 Hz. It supports the study of transfer learning for brain-computer interface skill acquisition, comparing unsupervised Generic Recentering and supervised Personally Assisted Recentering for calibration-free training. Participants performed left/right hand motor imagery with continuous visual feedback.
datasets.authors: Satyam Kumar, Hussein Alawieh, Frigyes Samuel Racz, Rawan Fakhreddine, Jose del R. Millan

datasets.name: Average Task Value
datasets.description: EEG dataset from twelve participants who completed three reinforcement learning tasks that differed in average task value. In each task, participants learned cue-response mappings for six coloured-shape cues, using left or right key presses. Cues had feedback validity of 0.5 (low-value) or 0.8 (high-value), and the tasks contained only low-value cues, only high-value cues, or a mix of both. The dataset supports investigation of how task-level value affects trial-level reward processing.
datasets.authors: Cameron D. Hassall, Laurence T. Hunt, Clay B. Holroyd

datasets.name: Somatosensory Cortex Rat DISC Data
datasets.description: Intracranial recordings from rat somatosensory cortex using the DISC (Directional and Scalable depth array) electrode array. Recordings were acquired under anesthesia while individual whiskers were stimulated with an air puffer, with each task name corresponding to the identity of the stimulated whisker. The dataset supports validation of the DISC array for sensing local field potentials.
datasets.authors: Amada Abrego, Wasif Khan, John P Seymour

datasets.name: BCIT Traffic Complexity
datasets.description: EEG and behavioral recordings from participants performing an extended simulated driving task with modulated visual complexity and perturbation frequency. The study aimed to identify driver fatigue and task performance changes through EEG-based biomarkers, compared against objective performance measures and a non-fatigued calibration driving session. It extends the Baseline Driving paradigm by adding pedestrians and traffic and varying how often lateral perturbations occurred.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Touryan (data and curation), Greg Apker (data), Brent Lance (data), Scott Kerick (data), Anthony Ries (data), Justin Brooks (data), Kaleb McDowell (data), Tony Johnson (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: BCIT Speed Control
datasets.description: EEG dataset from the Brain-Computer Interaction Technologies (BCIT) Speed Control study, in which participants performed extended, roughly 45-minute simulated driving sessions to assess fatigue-related changes in performance. Two conditions were compared: automatic constant speed with steering only (cruise) and manual control of both steering and speed. Lateral perturbations were applied to the vehicle, and the data support development of EEG-based biomarkers of driver fatigue alongside behavioral performance measures.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Touryan (data and curation), Greg Apker (data), Brent Lance (data), Scott Kerick (data), Anthony Ries (data), Justin Brooks (data), Kaleb McDowell (data), Tony Johnson (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: BCIT Mind Wandering
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a long-duration simulated driving study in which participants drove in a visually complex environment with lateral vehicle perturbations, a vigilance task (detecting police vehicles), and different background audio conditions (task-relevant, non-task-relevant, internal focus). The study aimed to identify markers of driver fatigue and mind wandering during prolonged time-on-task, in comparison with a non-fatigued calibration driving session. Data include 64-channel BioSemi EEG, eye tracking, and vehicle logs.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Touryan (data and curation), Greg Apker (data), Brent Lance (data), Scott Kerick (data), Anthony Ries (data), Justin Brooks (data), Kaleb McDowell (data), Tony Johnson (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: BCIT Baseline Driving
datasets.description: EEG recordings from a simulated driving study designed to assess fatigue-related changes in performance through EEG biomarkers. Participants completed a 60-minute driving task (six 10-minute blocks) with steering and speed control and periodic lateral perturbations. Data were collected at three sites (ARL, Teledyne, SAIC) using 64- or 256-channel BioSemi EEG systems. The dataset is part of the BCIT program and is a companion to the Calibration Driving session.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Touryan (data and curation), Greg Apker (data), Brent Lance (data), Scott Kerick (data), Anthony Ries (data), Kaleb McDowell (data), Tony Johnson (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: BCIT Basic Guard Duty
datasets.description: EEG dataset from the Basic Guard Duty study of the Brain-Computer Interaction Technologies (BCIT) collection, designed to measure sustained vigilance in a realistic setting. Participants verified replica ID cards against reference face photographs at varying queuing rates while 256-channel BioSemi EEG and eye tracking were recorded. The dataset is formatted in BIDS with HED annotations and accompanies companion calibration and baseline driving datasets.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Touryan (data and curation), Brent Lance (data), Scott Kerick (data), Anthony Ries (data), Kaleb McDowell (data), Tony Johnson (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: BCIT Calibration Driving
datasets.description: EEG and behavioral dataset from the Brain-Computer Interface Technologies (BCIT) Calibration Driving study, designed to provide baseline calibration data for fatigue-based driver performance prediction algorithms. Participants performed a 15-minute simulated driving task, correcting steering after periodic lateral perturbations, at three sites using identical driving simulators and 64- or 256-channel Biosemi EEG systems. The recordings serve as a non-fatigue performance reference for other BCIT studies collected in the same sessions.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Touryan (data and curation), Greg Apker (data), Brent Lance (data), Scott Kerick (data), Anthony Ries (data), Kaleb McDowell (data), Tony Johnson (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: Sternberg Working Memory
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 23 healthy young adults performing a modified Sternberg working memory task. Participants memorized a sequence of black letters while ignoring interspersed green letters, then judged whether a probe letter belonged to the memorized set and received auditory feedback. The dataset supports study of source-resolved frontal midline EEG dynamics during working memory encoding, maintenance, and retrieval, and is annotated with HED 8.0.0.
datasets.authors: Julie Onton (data), Scott Makeig (data and curation), Arnaud Delorme (data and curation), Dung Truong (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: MIND DATA
datasets.description: MEG dataset collected across multiple sites as part of a study on enabling cross-site pooling of magnetoencephalography data. The recordings were converted to BIDS using MNE-BIDS and follow the MEG-BIDS specification.
datasets.authors: M.P. Weisend, F.M. Hanlon, R. Montano, S.P. Ahlfors, A.C. Leuthold, D. Pantazis, J.C. Mosher, A.P. Georgopoulos, M.S. Hamalainen, C.J. Aine
